findings.title: Study 1: SD of .21 for total healthy choices contradicts the condition SDs 1.61 and 1.19
findings.description: Participants selected 5.6 healthy products out of 12 (SD = .21), which equals the two condition means summed (3.14 + 2.52). The SD of a sum of two variables with SDs 1.61 and 1.19 cannot be below their difference, 0.42, so SD = .21 cannot describe the same participants. Likely a typo or a different statistic, but the printed descriptive is inconsistent with the paper's own condition SDs.
findings.location: Study 1, Results, Descriptives vs Effects of a scarcity heuristic
findings.quote: participants selected an average of 5.6 healthy food products (SD = .21) out of the 12 food choice pairs

anchors.quote: participants selected an average of 5.6 healthy food products (SD = .21) out of the 12 food choice pairs
anchors.label: Descriptives

anchors.quote: more healthy choices were made in food pairs that had a scarcity heuristic (M = 3.14, SD = 1.61), compared to when there was no heuristic (M = 2.52, SD = 1.19)
anchors.label: Results paragraph 2

findings.notes: Assumes the 5.6 is the sum of the two 0-6 condition scores. If SD referred to something else (e.g. SE), the label is wrong instead.

findings.description: Participants selected 5.6 healthy products out of 12 (SD = .21), which equals the two condition means summed (3.14 + 2.52). The SD of a sum of two variables with SDs 1.61 and 1.19 cannot be below their difference, 0.42, so SD = .21 cannot describe the same participants. Likely a typo or a different statistic, but the printed descriptive is inconsistent with the paper's own condition SDs.
findings.location: Study 1, Results, Descriptives vs Effects of a scarcity heuristic
findings.quote: participants selected an average of 5.6 healthy food products (SD = .21) out of the 12 food choice pairs

anchors.quote: participants selected an average of 5.6 healthy food products (SD = .21) out of the 12 food choice pairs
anchors.label: Descriptives

anchors.quote: more healthy choices were made in food pairs that had a scarcity heuristic (M = 3.14, SD = 1.61), compared to when there was no heuristic (M = 2.52, SD = 1.19)
anchors.label: Results paragraph 2

findings.notes: Assumes the 5.6 is the sum of the two 0-6 condition scores. If SD referred to something else (e.g. SE), the label is wrong instead.

findings.title: Study 2: DV said to range 0-6 but only five trade-off pairs were analysed
findings.description: Methods state five of eight product pairs were hedonic-utilitarian trade-off pairs (three fillers not analysed), yet the dependent variable, number of utilitarian choices, is said to range from 0 to 6. With five pairs the maximum is 5. Either the pair count or the stated range is wrong, and it is unclear what was actually analysed.
findings.quote: The dependent variable was the number of utilitarian choices made from the trade-off product pairs, ranging from 0 to 6.

anchors.quote: five out of the eight product pairs were hedonic–utilitarian trade-off pairs
anchors.label: Product choice task, paragraph 1

anchors.quote: The dependent variable was the number of utilitarian choices made from the trade-off product pairs, ranging from 0 to 6.
anchors.label: Product choice task, paragraph 3

findings.title: Study 2: error df 147 does not match the analysed N of 155 in a 2x3 design
findings.description: Flow arithmetic holds (165 minus 5 minus 5 = 155 analysed). But a 2x3 between-subjects ANOVA on 155 participants has 155 - 6 = 149 error df, whereas the paper reports F(1, 147) and F(2, 147), implying N = 153. Two analysed participants are unaccounted for. Cell sizes are never reported.
findings.quote: The resulting sample in the analysis consisted of 155 participants.

anchors.quote: The resulting sample in the analysis consisted of 155 participants.
anchors.label: Results paragraph 1

findings.notes: A flow check on the printed exclusions passes; the discrepancy is between N and the printed df. The innocent explanation is a further unreported exclusion or typo.

findings.title: Study 1: error df 58 does not fit N = 67 with four covariates
findings.description: Study 1 reports 67 participants (64 with demographics). The repeated-measures ANCOVA has self-control, NFC and two further covariates, so error df would be N - 5: 62 for N = 67, 59 for N = 64. The reported df of 58 implies N = 63, and the paper reports no exclusions or missing-data handling for the analysis.
findings.quote: Participants were 67 individuals living in the United States recruited through Amazon’s Mechanical Turk.

anchors.quote: Participants were 67 individuals living in the United States recruited through Amazon’s Mechanical Turk.
anchors.label: Study 1 Participants

findings.notes: Assumes the model had self-control, NFC and two consumer-characteristic covariates as described; a different covariate set would change the expected df.

findings.title: Study 2: claim that demand scarcity beat supply scarcity rests on no significant demand-vs-supply difference
findings.description: The Discussion says support was obtained that demand scarcity would outperform supply scarcity. The Results show only demand vs no heuristic (p = .04, low self-control), with supply not differing from either (all ps > .21), and the omnibus interaction only p = .06 and heuristic main effect null. No demand-vs-supply contrast is significant, and the simple-effects tests are uncorrected. The abstract and conclusion repeat the superiority claim.
findings.location: Study 2 Results vs Discussion, Abstract, Conclusion
findings.quote: In Study 2, we obtained support for the hypothesis that a demand scarcity heuristic would outperform a supply scarcity heuristic in promoting more practical utilitarian products

anchors.quote: In Study 2, we obtained support for the hypothesis that a demand scarcity heuristic would outperform a supply scarcity heuristic in promoting more practical utilitarian products
anchors.label: Study 2 Discussion

anchors.quote: The supply scarcity heuristic (M = 1.17, SD = .94) did not differ from the other two conditions, all ps > .21.
anchors.label: Study 2 Results

findings.notes: The authors do not hedge. Also, the low-self-control demand vs no-heuristic contrast is interpreted despite an omnibus interaction at p = .06, and 'no difference' (p = .65) between high and low self-control under demand scarcity is read as a protective effect.

findings.title: Stroop manipulation durations are inconsistent with the stated trial timings and are confounded
findings.description: Each trial is given as 500 ms fixation + 200 ms word + 800 ms response window (1.5 s). 300 trials is then about 7.5 minutes, not the stated approximately 15, and 30 trials about 45 s, not approximately 5 minutes. The high-control condition also had only congruent trials and a different length, so the manipulation is confounded with duration and difficulty. No manipulation check is reported.
findings.quote: participants performed a total of 300 trials divided over three blocks, where two-thirds of the trials were incongruent trials dispersed randomly throughout the task

anchors.quote: Every trial began with a fixation cross at the center of the screen (500 ms), followed by the presentation of the color word (200 ms), and participants had 800 ms to indicate the font color
anchors.label: Self-control

anchors.quote: The length of the low self-control condition was approximately 15 minutes.
anchors.label: Self-control

findings.notes: Inter-trial gaps or block breaks not described could account for part of the discrepancy.

findings.title: Study 1: scarcity tag always on the same six healthy items, not counterbalanced
findings.description: The scarcity tagline was attached only to the healthy option in six fixed pairs; the other six pairs had no tag. Because each pair appeared once with or without the tag and assignment was not counterbalanced, the scarcity effect on healthy choices is confounded with pair content and with the tag being shown only next to the healthy item. Self-control was self-reported and covariates were retained because they correlated with the DV.
findings.quote: each food pair was only presented once with (or without) a scarcity heuristic and not counterbalanced

anchors.quote: The scarcity heuristic was presented in six of the food product pairs in the food choice task, and it was always associated with the healthy food option.
anchors.label: Scarcity

anchors.quote: each food pair was only presented once with (or without) a scarcity heuristic and not counterbalanced
anchors.label: Study 1 Discussion

findings.notes: The authors acknowledge the lack of counterbalancing as a limitation but still draw causal conclusions in the General discussion.

findings.title: Study 1: four consumer-characteristic questions stated, only three described
findings.description: Procedure refers to four questions assessing consumer characteristics, and the Method says participants answered four one-time questions, but only three questions are listed and used as covariates. One item appears to be missing or unreported.
findings.location: Study 1, Design and procedure vs Consumer characteristics
findings.quote: Participants responded to these four one-time questions on a 7-point scale ranging from 1 (never) to 7 (always).

anchors.quote: Participants responded to these four one-time questions on a 7-point scale ranging from 1 (never) to 7 (always).
anchors.label: Consumer characteristics

anchors.quote: The scores to each of the three questions were standardized.
anchors.label: Consumer characteristics

findings.title: Study 2 exclusion cascade 165 - 5 - 5 = 155 reconciles
findings.description: The printed Study 2 cascade (165 recruited, 5 excluded for missing Stroop data, 5 for 0 percent accuracy, 155 analysed) reconciles exactly. This covers only these counts, not the df discrepancy.
findings.quote: Five participants who had missing data in the Stroop Task and five other participants who performed the Stroop Task with an accuracy of 0 percent were excluded in the analyses.

anchors.quote: Five participants who had missing data in the Stroop Task and five other participants who performed the Stroop Task with an accuracy of 0 percent were excluded in the analyses.
